title: Indian ministry mulls integrating eri silk with Rajasthan’s Kota doria
summary:
India’s Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region is mulling over the possibility of integrating eri silk with Kota doria fabric of Rajasthan state to develop a premium handloom fabric for domestic and global markets. 
The initiative is expected to be formalised through an MoU between the North Eastern Handicrafts and Handlooms Development Corporation and Rajasthan’s District Industries Centre.

title: Italy’s imports grow 4.8% MoM in March amid trade rebound
summary:
Italy’s foreign trade strengthened in March 2026, with exports rising 4.1 per cent and imports 4.8 per cent MoM. 
Exports grew 7.4 per cent and imports 8 per cent YoY. 
The country recorded a €4.709 billion (~$5.462 billion) trade surplus, rising to €8.643 billion (~$10.026 billion) excluding energy. 
Import prices increased 2.5 per cent monthly but edged up only 0.1 per cent annually.

title: ICE cotton rebounds sharply on hopes of improving US-China ties
summary:
ICE cotton futures rebounded sharply after last week’s steep losses, supported by bullish macro sentiment, a weaker US dollar, stronger grain markets and hopes of improving US-China agricultural trade relations.
July futures gained 3.83 per cent, recovering nearly half of recent losses, while aggressive short-covering and positive commodity sentiment boosted buying interest.

title: UK growth to slow to 1% in 2026 amid Middle East war: IMF
summary:
The UK economy is projected to slow to 1 per cent growth in 2026 as the Middle East war raises energy prices and weakens consumer spending, as per the IMF. 
Inflation may peak just below 4 per cent by year-end, delaying its return to target until end-2027. 
Policymakers are urged to keep monetary policy restrictive, fiscal support targeted, and reforms focused on productivity.

title: China’s industrial output rises 5.6% in January-April 2026
summary:
China’s value-added industrial output rose 5.6 per cent year-on-year in January-April 2026, with April output up 4.1 per cent and 0.05 per cent month-on-month. 
Manufacturing grew 5.8 per cent, mining 5.5 per cent, and utilities 4.5 per cent, indicating steady industrial momentum across major production sectors and continued expansion among large enterprises.

title: Uzbekistan, China sign MoU to digitalise textile sector
summary:
Uztextileprom and China’s Shaoxing Huangxi Intelligent Group have signed an MoU to support digitalisation and modernisation of Uzbekistan’s textile industry. 
The partnership will focus on automation, digital solutions, technical consultations, experience sharing and pilot projects to improve production efficiency and raise the technological level of textile enterprises.

title: China’s retail sales rise 1.9% in January-April 2026
summary:
China’s retail sales of consumer goods rose 1.9 per cent year-on-year to 16.49 trillion yuan (~$2.41 trillion) in January-April 2026, while sales excluding automobiles grew 3.1 per cent to 15.2 trillion yuan. 
Rural sales outpaced urban growth, services rose 5.6 per cent, and online retail sales increased 6.6 per cent to 6.53 trillion yuan, signalling steady digital and service-led consumption momentum.

title: US industrial production up 0.7% in April 2026
summary:
US industrial production increased by 0.7 per cent in April this year after decreasing by 0.3 per cent in March, according to the Federal Reserve. 
In April, manufacturing output rose by 0.6 per cent after edging up by 0.1 per cent in March. 
The capacity utilisation of textile mills was 71.1 per cent in April and that of the apparel and leather industry was 66.2 per cent.

title: North India cotton yarn shows mixed trend amid cautious demand
summary:
North India’s cotton yarn market showed a mixed trend, with Ludhiana prices rising due to stronger export demand and higher mill selling rates, while Delhi remained steady amid cautious buying.
Panipat recycled yarn prices were unchanged as weak home textile demand and geopolitical uncertainty curbed export orders, while cotton prices paused after recent ICE cotton losses.

title: Cambodia’s apparel exports rise 9.6% in January-April 2026
summary:
Cambodia’s apparel exports rose 9.61 per cent to $3.45 billion in January–April 2026, accounting for 31.1 per cent of total exports and reaffirming the sector’s importance to the economy.
Strong April growth and gains across knitted and woven apparel reflected resilient sourcing demand, while rising cotton imports signalled changing raw-material preferences among manufacturers.

title: US’ Aramark’s Q2 revenue grows on US, international gains
summary:
Aramark has reported revenue of $4.9 billion in Q2 FY26, up 15 per cent YoY, driven by new business wins and growth across US and international operations. 
Operating income rose 26 per cent to $220 million, while adjusted EPS grew 40 per cent. 
Cash flow strengthened, client retention exceeded 98 per cent, and the company raised its organic revenue outlook.

title: Why Spring/Summer 2026 fashion colours reflect global chaos
summary:
Spring/Summer 2026 fashion is balancing bold and neutral palettes, with tomato red emerging as the standout colour alongside shades such as lost lilac, moody blue, soured citrus and jaded teal.  
Industry experts say earthy neutrals are becoming wardrobe foundations, while brighter tones are increasingly used as accents to add energy, nostalgia and emotional appeal.

title: South Korea’s Misto Holdings Q1 revenue rises 4.2% to $867.3 mn
summary:
Misto Holdings has reported a strong Q1 2026, with consolidated revenue rising 4.2 per cent YoY to KRW 1.3 trillion (~$867.3 million) and operating profit increasing 19 per cent to KRW 193.7 billion.

title: Mandate govt garment procurement from Ghanaian producers: AGAM
summary:
The Association of Ghana Apparel Manufacturers (AGAM) recently called for a national procurement policy for garments and textiles, saying such a step may create over 100,000 jobs.

summary:

GMV rose 5 per cent YoY to ₹19,666 crore (~$2.04 billion), while consolidated topline grew 4 per cent to ₹13,110 crore (~$1.36 billion). 
PAT stood at ₹178 crore (~$18.49 million), with gross margin improving to 20.6 per cent. 
The company also strengthened its cash flow and reduced debt.

title: Brazil’s apparel imports rise 19% amid growing reliance on China
summary:
Brazil’s apparel imports rose 19 per cent year-on-year to $833.75 million in Q1 2026, driven mainly by strong demand for man-made fibre and knitwear products.
China further strengthened its dominance, supplying over 60 per cent of imports, highlighting Brazil’s growing dependence on Chinese sourcing despite global diversification efforts.

title: Rising costs push Sri Lankan apparel SMEs to the edge
summary:
Sri Lanka’s apparel industry is facing mounting pressure as exports reportedly fell around 8 per cent in Q1 2026 amid weak global demand, rising fuel and electricity costs, shipping disruptions and geopolitical uncertainty. 
Smaller manufacturers are being hit hardest, with industry bodies urging urgent policy support, energy reforms and stronger trade access to stabilise the sector.

title: UK’s clothing exports dip 7.8% to $884 mn in January-March 2026
summary:
